_about: The AES walk's words (docs/walkthrough-design.md sections 2.2, 2.2c, 2.6). acceptance/checks/docs_checks.py scans this file for the phrases of section 2.6 and for the field definition lines.
fill: This is the block: 16 bytes of the text. They go down the columns, 4 bytes to a column. Next adds one byte.
decryptStart: Encrypt is done, and this is the locked block. Decrypt now runs the inverse steps, in reverse order, to get the text back.

steps.AddRoundKey: Each byte is XORed with the byte in the same place of round key {round}.
steps.SubBytes: Each byte is looked up in the S-box table, and the value there takes its place.
steps.ShiftRows: Row 0 stays. Row 1 moves 1 place to the left, row 2 moves 2, and row 3 moves 3. Bytes that leave on the left come back on the right.
steps.MixColumns: Each column is multiplied by a fixed matrix in the AES field, so every byte of a column now depends on all 4 bytes of that column.
steps.InvShiftRows: Each row moves back to the right by the places ShiftRows moved it to the left.
steps.InvSubBytes: Each byte is looked up in the inverse S-box table, which undoes the S-box.
steps.InvMixColumns: Each column is multiplied by the inverse matrix, which undoes MixColumns.

closed: Show keys is off. These steps show the key and the round keys, so they stay closed. Turn Show keys on to walk them. The S-box table, the key size table, the round constants, the field definition, and the modes walk stay open.
definition: A field is a set of values with add, subtract, multiply and divide, where every answer stays in the set. Only divide by zero is not allowed. They follow the usual rules of arithmetic.
A finite field has a fixed number of values. Another name for it is a Galois field. The field that AES uses has 256 values, one for each byte. Its name is GF(2^8).
Multiply treats each byte as a polynomial, multiplies without carries, and reduces the result by x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x + 1 (11b in hex). So the answer always fits in a byte.
Every value except zero has an inverse. So multiplying by any nonzero value can be undone.
